subject: Kestrel Health - streaming chat socket degradation during peak traffic
messages:
From: Julia Park <julia@kestrelhealth.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: 9/14 peak: SSE connections dropping + p99 spike

Diego —

We're seeing a sustained regression during our morning peak (08:30–09:10 PT): SSE clients experience intermittent disconnects and p99 latency on the streaming chat endpoint jumped from ~750ms to ~2.4s. Error rate for stream responses rose to ~4% and a number of sessions failed to reconnect automatically. This is hitting our triage dashboard and causing user-facing degradation.

I've attached the truncated logs and a short packet capture (kestrel_stream_logs_0914.zip). Key notes:
- Affected region: us-west-2
- Model: rwd-chat-medium-2027-08 (hosted)
- Traffic pattern: sudden spike in concurrent streams starting 08:27, sustained +80% above baseline for 20 minutes
- Observed: increased 503s for initial SSE handshake, then timeouts mid-stream

Can you triage urgently and advise mitigations? Our support rotation has been poking the app-level retry logic but we need platform confirmation. We're available for a call now.

Thanks,
Julia Park
Platform Ops — Kestrel Health
Attachments: kestrel_stream_logs_0914.zip (log bundle)

Subject: Re: 9/14 peak: SSE connections dropping + p99 spike

Julia —

Thanks for the quick report and the logs. I’m looping in SRE and the on-call infra engineers (Hannah + Rishi) to triage immediately. We can spin up a short triage call — joining now.

Immediate steps I’m asking team to evaluate:
1) Check autoscaler behavior for the dedicated pool serving rwd-chat-medium-2027-08 in us-west-2 and confirm if a scaling throttle or queueing backlog triggered.
2) Validate whether a new kernel or runtime change rolled out to that pool between 08:00–09:00 PT.
3) Evaluate routing fallback to the compatible variant (rwd-chat-small-2027-06) for connections that time out.

Julia, if you can provisionally flip traffic to the fallback endpoint for a small percentage, that may reduce user impact while we diagnose. I’ll keep you posted within the hour.

— Diego
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
To: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-14T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: initial triage notes (Kestrel)

Diego / Team —

Quick summary from the triage call and initial instrumentation:
- Autoscaler: no scaling-rejection events, but observed slow scale-up (instances added at ~09:01 despite CPU queue metrics signaling at ~08:29). Suspect eviction backoff and scheduler contention in the dedicated pool for us-west-2.
- Runtime: a targeted runtime kernel tweak was deployed to 3 host groups at 07:58 PT (rel-note: batch-optimizer v1.3). Canary passed on low-concurrency tests, but we see increased per-token latency under high concurrent streams on affected hosts.
- Network: no widespread infra network outages; packet traces show successful handshakes followed by elevated TLS renegotiations in ~18% of sessions.

Action items started:
- Rolling rollback of batch-optimizer v1.3 on the affected host groups (in progress).
- Temporarily route 15% of Kestrel traffic to rwd-chat-small-2027-06 (lower throughput footprint) — request to networking underway.
- Opened JIRA: JIRA-RT-1147 to track root cause and hotfix.

Hannah (SRE)

Date: 2027-09-15T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Executive note & proposed remediation/credits for Kestrel Health

Team / Julia —

Synthesis and ask for leadership:
1) What happened: a targeted runtime change (batch-optimizer v1.3) reduced efficiency under sustained high concurrent SSE workloads on a subset of us-west-2 host groups. This triggered elevated token latency under load and delayed autoscaler responsiveness, producing increased handshake errors and mid-stream timeouts for Kestrel's peak window on 9/14 (08:27–08:50 PT).
2) Mitigation performed: rollback completed 09:12 PT on 9/14; immediate routing of 15% traffic to rwd-chat-small applied at 09:22 PT. Post-rollback metrics show p99 for streams reduced from ~2.4s down to ~820ms within 20 minutes, and error rate fell from ~4% to 0.4% for observed sessions. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.example.com/dashboards/streams/kestrel-traffic
3) Next steps (engineering): finish postmortem with kernel microbenchmarks, expand canary tests for concurrency, and implement autoscaler smoothing improvements to avoid delayed scale events. JIRA: JIRA-RT-1147
4) Commercial ask: recommend offering Kestrel Health a discretionary credit for the affected window and a committed remediation timeline. Suggested credit: 10% of September hosted usage for Kestrel (subject to approval).

Julia — can you confirm whether the 15% fallback routing and rollback fully resolved the customer-visible issues on your end?

Asks for leadership: please approve the 10% credit and assign a small cross-functional postmortem team (runtime + autoscale) to deliver remediation plan in two weeks.

— Diego
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
